# VRFEditorGUI

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.UI` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/interaction/physics-hold/Editor/UI/VRFEditorGUI.cs#L11)

The drawing vocabulary shared by every VRF inspector: one header strip, collapsible section
boxes, and the notices that explain a multi-object selection. Editors call these instead of
hand-rolling boxes so the whole framework keeps one look.

```csharp
public static class VRFEditorGUI
```

### BandRegion(float, float) {#bandregion-single-single}

Confines the full-width bands to a region, for hosts that are not the Inspector.

The default spans `EditorGUIUtility.currentViewWidth`, which is right in an
inspector but not in the Project Settings window: there the view is the whole window,
category tree included, so a band would paint well past the page it belongs to. A host
in that position measures its own content width and declares it here.

```csharp
public static VRFEditorGUI.BandRegionScope BandRegion(float x, float width)
```

### HeaderBar(string, string, int) {#headerbar-string-string-int32}

Title strip at the top of an inspector: component name, optional one-line description,
and a badge when more than one object is selected.

Deliberately icon-free. Only some framework modules ship artwork, so an icon slot
would look complete on a handful of inspectors and empty on the rest; the accent rule
and the section markers carry the identity instead.

```csharp
public static void HeaderBar(string title, string subtitle, int selectionCount = 1)
```

### TagField(SerializedProperty, string) {#tagfield-serializedproperty-string}

Tag popup bound to a string property. Unlike a raw `EditorGUILayout.TagField`on a
field, this writes through the property, so it applies to every selected object and shows
the mixed-value dash when they disagree.
